answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a separate registered legal entity, verified against a public registry before it can trade. The entity's owners carry liability for what the agent does, so a banned name leaves its filing exposed and its owners answerable in court. A forger hiding behind a lagoon registry still leaves a paper trail. Each filing names its owners, and each agent must sit at a different vertex of that ownership graph, so one walnut-shell company cannot cover two names. Ten puppets mean ten filings, ten liabilities, ten exposures.
